title: Mid-Ocean Ridges
objective: After this level you can explain the longest mountain range on Earth.
summary: The mid-ocean ridge winds about 65,000 km around the globe, about 90% underwater: a chain of volcanoes where plates part and magma builds new sea floor. Marie Tharp found its central valley in 1952.

cards.headline: In 1952, Marie Tharp found a valley splitting an undersea mountain range.
cards.body: At Columbia University's Lamont lab, she was turning echo soundings of the Atlantic floor into profiles. Down the middle of an undersea mountain range, the profiles kept showing the same V-shaped notch. What could split a mountain range down the middle?

cards.headline: The longest mountain range on Earth
cards.body: Tharp was looking at one stretch of the mid-ocean ridge. It winds about 65,000 km around the globe, like the stitches on a baseball, which makes it the longest mountain range on Earth. And about 90% of it lies under the ocean. Earth's longest mountain range, and you've probably never seen it.

cards.headline: A mountain range that builds sea floor
cards.body: The ridge is the largest single volcanic feature on Earth: thousands of volcanoes and volcanic ridge segments that erupt from time to time. It rises from sea floor about 5 km deep to crests about 2.6 km below the surface. Along it, plates push apart and magma rises to fill the gap, building brand-new sea floor. The ridge isn't just scenery. It's a factory.

cards.headline: "Girl talk"
cards.body: Tharp's colleague Bruce Heezen at first dismissed her valley as "girl talk". By 1953 he was convinced: the locations of earthquakes turned out to line up inside it. The valley was real, and it ran right along the seam where the plates push apart. Tharp had found where the sea floor is made.

mascot.line: Dismissed as girl talk, confirmed by earthquakes. Trust the data, and the person who plotted it.

questions.prompt: What sets the mid-ocean ridge apart from Earth's other mountain ranges?

options.label: It's the tallest, rising higher than Everest
options.rationale: It's the longest, not the tallest.

options.label: It's the oldest, older than every continent
options.rationale: Its rock is new sea floor, not old.

options.label: It's the longest, and about 90% is underwater
It's the only range made mostly of ice

questions.explanation: The mid-ocean ridge winds about 65,000 km around the globe, Earth's longest mountain range, and about 90% of it is underwater.

questions.prompt: What happens along the mid-ocean ridge that builds new sea floor?

options.label: Rivers drop mud that hardens into rock
options.rationale: The ridge is volcanic; mud isn't the builder.

options.label: Plates push apart and magma rises to fill the gap
Two plates collide and one dives under
Coral reefs pile up into mountains
options.rationale: The ridge is made of volcanoes, not coral.

questions.explanation: Along the ridge, plates push apart and magma rises to fill the gap, building brand-new sea floor.

questions.prompt: From Level 11: what did Marie Tharp turn into profiles to spot a valley kilometers under the Atlantic?

options.label: Photographs taken by divers on the floor
options.rationale: No light or diver reached that deep.

options.label: Echo soundings: timed echoes of sound off the floor
Satellite pictures of the sea surface
options.rationale: Her profiles came from echo soundings.

options.label: Lead-line ropes dropped across the ocean
options.rationale: Sonar echoes, not ropes, gave her profiles.

questions.explanation: Tharp turned echo soundings, depths from timed sound echoes, into profiles of the Atlantic floor.
